\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Adjacency in an encoded graph]
\lean{FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent}
\label{FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.GraphEdge}
Let $v$ be a natural number, let $G$ encode a graph on the vertex set $\{0,\ldots,v-1\}$
by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex set, and let $u,w$ be vertices.
Then $u$ and $w$ are adjacent in $G$ precisely when they are distinct and some
two-element set assigned value true contains both of them.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Adjacency under vertex relabeling]
\lean{FABL.encodedGraphAdjacent_permute_iff}
\label{FABL.encodedGraphAdjacent_permute_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent, FABL.graphEdgePermEquiv, FABL.permuteEncodedGraph}
\difficulty{4}
Let $v$ be a natural number, let $G$ assign a Boolean value to each two-element subset
of the $v$ vertices, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the vertices, and let $u,w$ be
vertices. The vertices $\sigma(u)$ and $\sigma(w)$ are adjacent in the relabeled graph
if and only if $u$ and $w$ are adjacent in $G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Adjacency is monotone under edge inclusion]
\lean{FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent.mono}
\label{FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent.mono}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent, FABL.EncodedGraphLE}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ and $H$ be Boolean encodings of graphs on the same finite vertex set, with every
edge present in $G$ also present in $H$. If two vertices are distinct and adjacent in
$G$, then they are adjacent in $H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Connected encoded graph]
\lean{FABL.EncodedGraphConnected}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.EncodedGraphConnected}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent}
For a natural number $v$, an encoded graph on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$ is
connected if, for every pair of vertices, there is a finite chain of vertices from the
first to the second in which each consecutive pair is adjacent according to the encoded
graph.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {FABL.EncodedGraphConnected}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p224-b001}
Let $G$ and $H$ be Boolean encodings of graphs on the same finite vertex set, with every
edge present in $G$ also present in $H$. If every pair of vertices in $G$ is joined by a
finite path, then every pair of vertices in $H$ is joined by a finite path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Colorable encoded graph]
\lean{FABL.EncodedGraphColorable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.EncodedGraphColorable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent}
For natural numbers $v$ and $q$, an encoded graph on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$
is colorable with $q$ colors if its vertices can be assigned colors from a set of $q$
colors so that every adjacent pair receives distinct colors.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Colorability under vertex relabeling]

\proofstep
  {FABL.EncodedGraphColorable}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006}
Let $v,q$ be natural numbers, let $G$ assign a Boolean value to each two-element subset
of the $v$ vertices, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the vertices. The graph
obtained by relabeling $G$ by $\sigma$ admits a proper coloring with $q$ colors if and
only if $G$ admits a proper coloring with $q$ colors.
\end{theorem}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005}
Let $G$ and $H$ be Boolean encodings of graphs on the same finite vertex set, and let
$q$ be a natural number. If every edge present in $G$ is present in $H$ and $H$ has a
proper coloring with $q$ colors, then $G$ has a proper coloring with $q$ colors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Clique in an encoded graph]
\lean{FABL.EncodedGraphContainsClique}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b003,
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b005
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.EncodedGraphContainsClique}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphAdjacent}
Let $v$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $G$ assign a Boolean value to each
two-element subset of the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$. The graph encoded by $G$
contains a clique of size $k$ if there is a set $S$ of $k$ vertices such that every two
distinct vertices in $S$ are adjacent.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b003,
    pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b005}
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same finite vertex set, and suppose every edge of $G$
is also an edge of $H$. If $G$ contains a clique of size $k$, then $H$ contains a clique
of size $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Connectivity property of an encoded graph]
\lean{FABL.connectivityGraphProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.connectivityGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphConnected}
Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set
$\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex
set. The connectivity property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $G$
is connected.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Connectivity Is Invariant Under Relabeling]
\lean{FABL.connectivity_isGraphProperty}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.connectivity_isGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsGraphProperty, FABL.connectivityGraphProperty, FABL.encodedGraphConnected_permute_iff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $v$ be a natural number, and encode a simple graph on the vertex set
$\{0,\ldots,v-1\}$ by a Boolean function on its two-element vertex subsets. The Boolean
property that every pair of vertices is joined by a path is invariant under every
permutation of the vertices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Connectivity is monotone graph property]
\lean{FABL.connectivity_isMonotoneGraphProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p224-b001}
\label{FABL.connectivity_isMonotoneGraphProperty}
\leanok

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-colorability property]
\lean{FABL.threeColorableGraphProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.threeColorableGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphColorable}
Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set
$\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex
set. The three-colorability property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly
when the vertices of $G$ can be colored with three colors so that adjacent vertices
receive different colors.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Three colorable is graph property]
\lean{FABL.threeColorable_isGraphProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.threeColorable_isGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsGraphProperty, FABL.encodedGraphColorable_permute_iff, FABL.threeColorableGraphProperty}
\difficulty{3}
% dataset-pipeline: stub -- prose pending build_informal_statements.py
Statement pending regeneration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Failure of three-colorability]
\lean{FABL.notThreeColorableGraphProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p224-b001
}
\label{FABL.notThreeColorableGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphColorable}
Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set
$\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex
set. The non-three-colorability property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true
exactly when $G$ cannot be properly colored with three colors.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Non-three-colorability is invariant under relabeling]

  {FABL.notThreeColorableGraphProperty}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005}
For every natural number $v$, the Boolean property of a graph on $v$ vertices that holds
exactly when the graph is not three-colorable is invariant under every permutation of
the vertices.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.notThreeColorableGraphProperty}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p224-b001}
For any fixed number $v$ of vertices, regard a graph on the vertex set
$\{0,\ldots,v-1\}$ as a choice of edges, each an unordered pair of distinct vertices. If
such a graph $G$ has no proper coloring with three colors, then every graph on the same
vertex set containing all the edges of $G$ also has no proper coloring with three
colors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Clique containment property]
\lean{FABL.containsCliqueGraphProperty}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b003,
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p008-b005
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.containsCliqueGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.EncodedGraph, FABL.EncodedGraphContainsClique}
Let $v$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set
$\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex
set. The clique-containment property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly
when $G$ contains a clique of size $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Clique existence is invariant under vertex relabeling]
\lean{FABL.containsClique_isGraphProperty}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006
}
\label{FABL.containsClique_isGraphProperty}
\leanok

  {FABL.containsCliqueGraphProperty}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006}
For any natural numbers $v$ and $k$, the Boolean property that a graph on $v$ vertices
contains a clique of size $k$ is invariant under every permutation of its vertices.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.containsCliqueGraphProperty}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p223-b006}
For any natural numbers $v$ and $k$, if a graph on $v$ vertices contains a clique of
size $k$, then every graph on the same vertices whose edge set contains the first
graph's edge set also contains a clique of size $k$.
\end{theorem}
